Hi Liam — thanks for the time today. Quick written recap so we have a tidy handoff and clear next steps.

Key points from the call (short):

- Traffic profile (ballpark): you mentioned ~120–160 TPS steady for chat endpoints, with ~500–650 TPS peak during promotions.
- Token mix: median requests ~120 tokens, average ~350 tokens, ~10% long-context (>800 tokens).
- Models: you're evaluating Llama-2-family & Falcon-style open models; interested in using a 70B-class for higher-quality responses.

Attachments: I attached a capacity worksheet (sundry_capacity_worksheet.xlsx) — could you fill the peaktime breakdown per endpoint and expected growth for the next 6 months? That will let us map to GPU pool sizing.

Open questions we promised to follow up on:
- H100 vs A100 tradeoffs (cost vs single-request latency for large-context workloads).
- How important is homogeneous hardware vs mixed-pool? (i.e., do you want a single SKU for simplicity or a small H100 burst pool?)
- Any hard SLA/uptime or compliance constraints beyond SOC2? (e.g., regional data residency).

Next steps I propose:

2) We do an internal sizing + cost estimate (I’ll loop Karthik and Marissa).
3) Quick 30-min follow-up next week to review recommended pool and pricing.

Thanks again — I’ll line up the internal sizing once we get the worksheet.

Thanks Priyom — useful recap. A few clarifications to make the worksheet more accurate:

- Steady-state TPS: plan on ~160 TPS across the chat API (this is after we shard some traffic to a cheap hosted endpoint for low-sensitivity interactions).
- Peak events: during promotions we see spikes to ~600 TPS for ~20–40 minute windows (not sustained for hours).
- Token distribution: ~60% under 200 tokens, ~30% 200–800 tokens, ~10% >800 tokens (those are often summary/aggregation requests).
- Latency target: P95 < 350ms for chat median-sized requests, P99 ideally < 700ms.
- Compliance: SOC2+HIPAA is likely (we're finalizing scope). Data residency: US only for now.

On hardware: we prefer to prioritize cost but are open to an H100 option for the heavy tail (long-context and lower-latency). If H100 gives a notable latency win at reasonable cost delta, we can include it.

Thanks for the context — good profile. High-level sizing and rationale below (conservative).

Assumptions:
- Model: 70B open-family (quantized q4f16 or q8_0 where supported).
- Average tokens/request: 350, 10% long >800.
- Target P95 latency: <350ms for median requests.

Conservative baseline (cost-conscious):
- Primary pool: 6 x A100 80GB (dedicated nodes)
- Burst pool: 1 x A100 80GB with autoscale to 2 x A100 for short spikes
- Reasoning: A100 80GB gives best cost/throughput for quantized 70B models; with batching and KV caching we estimate 18–28 chat TPS per A100 for the stated token profile. 6 nodes -> ~108–168 TPS sustained depending on effective batching. Autoscale for short peaks.

Latency-optimized (recommended for headroom & long-context):
- Primary pool: 4 x A100 80GB
- Burst/HQ pool: 2 x H100 80GB (reserved for >400-token requests and promotion bursts)
- Reasoning: H100 delivers lower single-request latency and better long-context perf; two H100s handle the heavy tail and burst windows while the A100s handle steady traffic. With this mix and careful routing (route >400-token requests to HQ pool + prefix cache), we expect to meet P95 <350ms and P99 <700ms.

Operational items to include in proposal:
- KV/prefix caching plan for chat sessions to reduce token work on repeated context.
- Autoscaling thresholds and pre-warming: start scale-up at 65% pool utilization and pre-warm burst H100s on predictable promo windows.
- Canary and rollback policy to fall back to a cheaper hosted variant on sustained capacity pressure.

Next steps (internal):
- Marissa: cost estimate for both configurations (include committed monthly numbers and burst overage assumptions).
- Priyom: confirm whether we should include a short pilot (2–4 weeks) with reduced commitment and a buyout to full reserved capacity.

I'll draft a short slide with the sizing table; will push to the shared drive in an hour.
